name: i3
summary: Tiling window manager for X11 with a container tree (splits, tabbed, stacking), plain-text config and i3-msg IPC. Gaps are built in since 4.22 (the former i3-gaps fork was merged). No rounded corners or opacity without an external compositor.

install.notes: Window manager only; the i3 group adds i3status, i3lock, i3bar tools. The separate i3-gaps package no longer exists.
Metapackage (i3-wm, i3status, i3lock, suckless-tools). Debian unstable/testing carry 4.25.1; stable releases may carry older versions without gaps (4.22+ needed).

linux.notes: X11 only (no Wayland session; use sway for the same config on Wayland). Gaps need i3 4.22 or newer; before that they exist only in the i3-gaps fork. Newest version seen: 4.25.1 (from Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora package data, February 2026); i3wm.org was not checked for a newer tag. Config search order: ~/.config/i3/config (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/i3/config), ~/.i3/config, /etc/xdg/i3/config, /etc/i3/config. On first start i3 offers i3-config-wizard to create the config; if ~/.i3/config exists the wizard will not run. Transparency, rounded corners and shadows need an X11 compositor such as picom, which is a separate program.

borders.notes: Width and colors only. Rounded corners need an external X11 compositor.

window-rules.notes: for_window and assign cover float, size, position, border and workspace. There is no opacity command; transparency needs a compositor.
